gdp_nominal.note: BEA national accounts, calendar-year 1949 GDP in current dollars.

gdp_real.note: 1949 is the base year for real figures, so real GDP equals nominal GDP at the start.

real_growth.note: BEA, real GDP change for calendar 1949 (a mild recession year).

inflation.note: BLS CPI, annual-average change 1948 to 1949. Prices fell after the 1948 peak.

unemployment.note: BLS, average of Jan–Mar 1949 monthly rates. The rate climbed through 1949 to a peak near 7.9% in October.

budget_balance.note: OMB historical tables, fiscal 1949: receipts $39.4bn, outlays $38.8bn.

interest_rate.note: Three-month Treasury bill rate, 1949 average, held low by the Federal Reserve's wartime peg.

public_debt.note: OMB historical tables, federal debt held by the public at the end of fiscal 1949.

debt_to_gdp.note: Debt held by the public ($214.3bn) divided by 1949 GDP ($272.5bn).

gold_reserves.note: US monetary gold stock in 1949, close to its all-time peak of roughly $24.6bn.

steel_output.note: Raw steel output for 1949, about 78 million short tons (70.7 million metric tonnes).

defence_spending.note: OMB historical tables, national defence outlays for fiscal 1949.

active_personnel.note: Interpolated for January 1949 between 1.45 million (June 1948) and 1.62 million (June 1949) on active duty.

nuclear_warheads.note: Declassified US stockpile at the end of 1948. It reached about 170 by the end of 1949.

population.note: Interpolated for January 1949 from Census mid-year estimates: 146.6 million (1948) and 149.2 million (1949).

population_growth_annual.note: Mid-1948 to mid-1949 growth from Census estimates, including immigration. A placeholder until the cohort-component model replaces it.

fixed_investment.note: Business and residential fixed investment, 1949 (approximate BEA figure; check NIPA Table 1.1.5).

inventory_investment.note: Change in business inventories, early 1949. Over the full year firms ran stocks down by about $3bn.

government.note: Government consumption and investment, federal plus state and local, 1949 (approximate BEA figure).

exports.note: Exports of goods and services, 1949 (approximate BEA figure), much of it financed by US aid.

imports.note: Imports of goods and services, 1949 (approximate BEA figure).

output_gap.note: Output relative to potential, consistent with Okun's law given 4.7% unemployment and a 4.5% natural rate.

inventory_overhang.note: Excess stocks built up in the 1948 boom ($bn). Sized so the model reproduces the mild inventory recession of 1949.

net_factor_income.note: Net income from US investments abroad, 1949 (approximate).

private_capital_outflow.note: Net private US lending and investment abroad, 1949 (approximate).

unemployment_insurance.note: Unemployment benefits at early-1949 unemployment. Paid automatically and rises with joblessness.

debt_interest.note: Net interest on the federal debt, fiscal 1949 (OMB historical tables, approximate).

other_receipts.note: Miscellaneous federal receipts, fiscal 1949, after the tax lines below.

short_rate_ceiling.note: Under the wartime peg the Fed kept bill rates from rising much above about 1.25% to hold down the Treasury's borrowing costs. It could ease, but not tighten. The 1951 Treasury–Fed Accord ended this.

long_rate.note: Long-term Treasury yield, held under the Fed's 2.5% ceiling.

defence_abroad_share.note: Share of defence spending paid out at overseas bases and occupation zones, a drain on the balance of payments.

aid_tied_share.note: Share of foreign aid spent on American goods. Most Marshall Plan dollars bought US wheat, coal, machinery and fuel.

defence.note: OMB historical tables, national defence outlays, fiscal 1949.

foreign_aid.note: International affairs outlays, fiscal 1949, dominated by the Marshall Plan (approximate).

welfare.note: Veterans' benefits (about $6.7bn) plus public assistance and social security, fiscal 1949, excluding unemployment insurance (approximate).

infrastructure.note: Federal public works: transport, water, power and natural resources, fiscal 1949 (approximate).

research.note: Federal civilian research and the non-weapons side of atomic energy, fiscal 1949 (approximate).

education_health.note: Federal education and health grants, fiscal 1949. Most such spending was by the states (approximate).

general_government.note: Agriculture programmes, justice and administration, fiscal 1949 (approximate). Balances outlays to $38.8bn.

income.note: Individual income tax receipts as a share of household income, about 8% in 1949.

excise.note: Excise receipts as a share of consumer spending, 1949.

payroll.note: Social insurance receipts as a share of wages. Statutory rate 1% each on employer and employee, up to $3,000 of wages.

tariff.note: Customs duties as a share of all imports, 1949.

income.note: Individual income tax receipts, fiscal 1949 (OMB historical tables, approximate).
